summary.en: President De la Espriella is confronting multiple security crises as armed violence rises and a police academy attack killed 21 people, while protests over tax plans and spending cuts sweep the country. He ordered a tenth bombing against a narcoterrorist target in Valle del Cauca and called on the United States to prosecute former President Petro. U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth arrived in Bogotá, delivered a C-130, met De la Espriella, and announced a US-Venezuela military partnership, but Colombia rejected a U.S. proposal for joint anti-drug strikes. The conflict recorded 225 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
